let.gap: IF(CELL_COUNT("$Cars", 1, 0) > 0, 0, IF(CELL_COUNT("$Cars", 2, 0) > 0, 1, IF(CELL_COUNT("$Cars", 3, 0) > 0, 2, IF(CELL_COUNT("$Cars", 4, 0) > 0, 3, IF(CELL_COUNT("$Cars", 5, 0) > 0, 4, vmax)))))
let.vn: IF(UNIF(0, 1) < p and v1 > 0, v1 - 1, v1)

info.description: The Nagel-Schreckenberg traffic cellular automaton on a 60-cell ring (a 1-D torus grid, `size: [60, 1]`), its three rules written once as tick-local `let` values: `gap` (the free cells ahead, read by CELL_COUNT('$Cars', k, 0) for k = 1..5 -- an arbitrary-offset grid read), `v1 = min(v + 1, Vmax, gap)` (accelerate, then brake for the car ahead) and `vn`, v1 minus 1 with probability P when v1 > 0 -- ONE slowdown draw per car per tick, shared by the action that moves the car `vn` cells, the one that stores its speed and the one that records `flow_contrib = density * vn`, whose population mean IS the flow, with no derived-KPI step. Cars act in index order, which is ring order, so each reads the cells ahead before the car there moves (the parallel update NS defines); only the last car reads the first car's new cell across the wrap. With Vmax 5 and P 0.15 the flow-density curve peaks near density 0.1 (6 cars) and is far lower at density 0.8 (48 cars) -- the published shape. Vmax and P are this instance's own; the ring length and car count are fixed so the built-in oracle stays exact.

parameters.label: Max speed
parameters.help: Fastest a car can go, in cells/tick.

parameters.name: p
parameters.label: Slowdown probability
parameters.help: Chance a moving car randomly loses 1 speed each tick.

parameters.name: cars
parameters.label: Cars
parameters.help: Number of cars on the 60-cell ring (density = cars / 60). Car k starts on cell k -- one jam that dissolves during the warm-up -- so index order is ring order for any count.
